component.name: aws2-mq
component.title: AWS MQ
component.description: Create, describe, update, reboot, delete and list brokers in Amazon MQ.
component.label: cloud,management

configuration.description: The configuration that the endpoints of the component start from. Each endpoint uses a copy of it, in which its own URI options replace the values.

lazyStartProducer.label: producer
lazyStartProducer.description: Whether the producer should be started lazy (on the first message). By starting lazy you can use this to allow CamelContext and routes to startup in situations where a producer may otherwise fail during starting and cause the route to fail being started. By deferring this startup to be lazy then the startup failure can be handled during routing messages via Camel's routing error handlers. Beware that when the first message is processed then creating and starting the producer may take a little time and prolong the total processing time of the processing.

operation.description: The operation that the producer performs. The CamelAwsMQOperation header replaces this option.

overrideEndpoint.description: Whether to send the requests to the URI of the uriEndpointOverride option instead of the endpoint of the region. It has no effect when uriEndpointOverride is not set.

pojoRequest.description: Whether the body is the request object of the AWS SDK for the operation, such as a CreateBrokerRequest, which the producer sends as it is. The headers that give the input of the operation are then not used, and a body of another type fails the exchange.

region.description: The AWS region of Amazon MQ, as a region ID such as eu-west-1, which is the value of Region.EU_WEST_1.id(). If not set, the AWS SDK takes the region from its default region provider chain, for example the AWS_REGION environment variable.

uriEndpointOverride.description: The URI of the endpoint to use instead of the endpoint of the region, for example http://localhost:4566 for a local emulator. It is used only when overrideEndpoint is true.

amazonMqClient.label: advanced
amazonMqClient.description: To use a custom software.amazon.awssdk.services.mq.MqClient. When this option is set or autowired, the credentials, region, proxy, endpoint override and trustAllCertificates options are not used. The Camel endpoint does not close a client that is set or autowired.

autowiredEnabled.label: advanced
autowiredEnabled.description: Whether autowiring is enabled. This is used for automatic autowiring options (the option must be marked as autowired) by looking up in the registry to find if there is a single instance of matching type, which then gets configured on the component. This can be used for automatic configuring JDBC data sources, JMS connection factories, AWS Clients, etc.

healthCheckConsumerEnabled.label: health
healthCheckConsumerEnabled.description: Used for enabling or disabling all consumer based health checks from this component

healthCheckProducerEnabled.label: health
healthCheckProducerEnabled.description: Used for enabling or disabling all producer based health checks from this component. Notice: Camel has by default disabled all producer based health-checks. You can turn on producer checks globally by setting camel.health.producersEnabled=true.

proxyHost.label: proxy
proxyHost.description: The host name of the proxy that the HTTP client of Amazon MQ connects through. The proxy is used only when the proxyPort option is set too.

proxyPort.label: proxy
proxyPort.description: The port of the proxy that the HTTP client of Amazon MQ connects through. The proxy is used only when the proxyHost option is set too.

proxyProtocol.label: proxy
proxyProtocol.description: The protocol that the HTTP client of Amazon MQ uses to connect to the proxy. It is used only when the proxyHost and proxyPort options are set.

accessKey.label: security
accessKey.description: The access key ID of the AWS credentials, used together with the secretKey option. It is not used when useDefaultCredentialsProvider or useProfileCredentialsProvider is true.

profileCredentialsName.label: security
profileCredentialsName.description: The name of the profile in the AWS shared credentials and config files, used when useProfileCredentialsProvider is true. If not set, the AWS SDK uses its default profile, which the AWS_PROFILE environment variable can change.

secretKey.label: security
secretKey.description: The secret access key of the AWS credentials, used together with the accessKey option. It is not used when useDefaultCredentialsProvider or useProfileCredentialsProvider is true.

sessionToken.label: security
sessionToken.description: The session token of temporary AWS credentials, for example of an assumed IAM role. It is used only when useSessionCredentials is true, together with the accessKey and secretKey options.

trustAllCertificates.label: security
trustAllCertificates.description: Whether the HTTP client of Amazon MQ trusts every TLS certificate without checking it. It applies to any endpoint, not only to an overridden one, so use it only for testing, for example against a local emulator.

useDefaultCredentialsProvider.label: security
useDefaultCredentialsProvider.description: Whether to load the credentials with the default credentials provider chain of the AWS SDK, which looks in system properties, environment variables, the shared credentials and config files, and the container or instance role. It takes precedence over the other credentials options.

useProfileCredentialsProvider.label: security
useProfileCredentialsProvider.description: Whether to load the credentials from a profile of the AWS shared credentials and config files, the one of the profileCredentialsName option. It is not used when useDefaultCredentialsProvider is true, and it takes precedence over the session and static credentials.

useSessionCredentials.label: security
useSessionCredentials.description: Whether to use temporary credentials made of the accessKey, secretKey and sessionToken options, for example those of an assumed IAM role. It is not used when useDefaultCredentialsProvider or useProfileCredentialsProvider is true.

CamelAwsMQOperation.description: The operation that the producer performs. It replaces the operation option.

CamelAwsMQMaxResults.description: The maximum number of brokers in one page of listBrokers. Amazon MQ accepts a value from 5 to 100, and returns 20 brokers per page when it is not set.

CamelAwsMQBrokerName.description: The name of the broker that createBroker creates, which createBroker requires. Amazon MQ requires a name that is unique in the AWS account, 1 to 50 characters long, with only letters, digits, dashes and underscores.

CamelAwsMQBrokerEngine.description: The engine of the broker that createBroker creates: ACTIVEMQ or RABBITMQ, in upper case. createBroker requires it.

CamelAwsMQBrokerEngineVersion.description: The version of the engine of the broker that createBroker creates, which must be a version that Amazon MQ supports for the engine of the CamelAwsMQBrokerEngine header. createBroker requires it.

CamelAwsMQBrokerID.description: The ID of the broker that deleteBroker, rebootBroker, updateBroker and describeBroker act on, which they require. createBroker sets it to the ID of the new broker.

CamelAwsMQConfigurationID.description: The configuration that updateBroker applies to the broker: a ConfigurationId of the AWS SDK, with the ID and optionally the revision of the configuration, or the ID of the configuration as a String. updateBroker requires it.

CamelAwsMQBrokerDeploymentMode.description: The deployment mode of the broker that createBroker creates: SINGLE_INSTANCE, ACTIVE_STANDBY_MULTI_AZ for ActiveMQ, or CLUSTER_MULTI_AZ for RabbitMQ. createBroker requires it.

CamelAwsMQBrokerInstanceType.description: The instance type of the broker that createBroker creates, such as mq.t3.micro or mq.m5.large. createBroker requires it.

CamelAwsMQBrokerUsers.description: The users of the broker that createBroker creates, as a List of User of the AWS SDK, each with a username and a password. createBroker requires at least one user, and a RabbitMQ broker accepts exactly one administrative user.

CamelAwsMQBrokerPubliclyAccessible.description: Whether applications outside the VPC of the broker that createBroker creates can connect to it. When not set, createBroker creates a broker that is not publicly accessible.

CamelAwsMQNextToken.label: listBrokers
CamelAwsMQNextToken.description: The token of a page of listBrokers. listBrokers reads it to return that page instead of the first one, and sets it to the token of the next page, which has no value on the last page.

CamelAwsMQIsTruncated.label: listBrokers
CamelAwsMQIsTruncated.description: Whether listBrokers has more brokers after the returned page, that is whether the CamelAwsMQNextToken header has a value.

CamelAwsMQBrokerArn.label: createBroker describeBroker
CamelAwsMQBrokerArn.description: The Amazon Resource Name (ARN) of the broker that createBroker created or describeBroker described.

CamelAwsMQBrokerState.label: describeBroker
CamelAwsMQBrokerState.description: The state of the broker that describeBroker described, such as RUNNING, CREATION_IN_PROGRESS, REBOOT_IN_PROGRESS or CRITICAL_ACTION_REQUIRED.

producerIn.description: Not used: the operations take their input from headers, such as the id of the broker in CamelAwsMQBrokerID, and the users of createBroker as a List of the User of the AWS SDK. With pojoRequest=true the request of the AWS SDK for the operation, such as a ListBrokersRequest: another body fails

producerOut.description: The response of the AWS SDK for the operation, such as the ListBrokersResponse of listBrokers, with the token of the next page in a header
